jobs.title: Sourcing Program Manager
jobs.description:
Xylem is a Fortune 500 global water solutions company dedicated to advancing sustainable impact and empowering the people who make water work every day. As a leading water technology company with 23,000 employees operating in over 150 countries, Xylem is at the forefront of addressing the world's most critical water challenges. We invite passionate individuals to join our team, dedicated to exceeding customer expectations through innovative and sustainable solutions.

About Xylem:
Xylem, Inc. is a global leader in water technology, committed to creating sustainable solutions that address the world’s most complex water challenges. We develop innovative and efficient systems that improve how water is managed, conserved, and reused—across the globe.

Position Summary:
We are hiring a Sourcing Manager. As a Sourcing Manager, you will play a pivotal role in strengthening Xylem’s supply base, optimizing total cost of ownership, and delivering materials and services that enable manufacturing excellence and long-term competitiveness. The Sourcing Program Manager is responsible for developing and executing sourcing strategies that align with business objectives and support new product introduction (NPI), cost reduction, supplier quality and capability. This role manages the end-to-end strategic sourcing lifecycle, including supplier evaluation, contract negotiation, supplier development, and performance improvement.
This individual will lead cross-functional initiatives with Engineering, Operations, Quality, and Procurement teams to ensure a best-in-class, risk-mitigated, and value-driven supply base.

Key Responsibilities:
Sourcing Strategy
- Develop and implement commodity sourcing strategies aligned with global supply chain and product roadmap objectives.
- Drive sourcing projects and ensure they are completed on time, within scope, and within
-
- Monitor industry trends and identify sourcing opportunities that support cost competitiveness and innovation.

Supplier Development
- Identify and onboard high-performing suppliers to support business growth and mitigate risk.
- Collaborate with Quality and Operations to elevate supplier capabilities and ensure alignment with Xylem’s performance standards.

Supply Base Optimization
- Rationalize and consolidate the supplier base to reduce complexity and leverage economies of scale.
- Support dual-sourcing strategies and risk mitigation plans across key commodities and regions.

Negotiations & Agreements
- Lead supplier negotiations on pricing, terms, lead times, and contracts to drive favorable commercial outcomes.
- Develop, execute, and manage supplier agreements, including long-term supply and development contracts.

Pricing Maintenance & Cost Reduction
- Provide accurate pricing data for ERP systems and ensure alignment with contracts and forecasts.
- Lead cost reduction initiatives through value engineering, volume leverage, and alternative sourcing.

Supplier Selection & Assessment
- Responsible for awarding business to qualified suppliers to meet business need in alignment with engineering, quality and supply chain strategies and policies

- Execute fair and competitive sourcing processes (RFQ/RFP) and facilitate award decisions based on TCO (Total Cost of Ownership).
- Align sourcing strategy with financial, operational and risk mitigation goals.
- Collaborate with suppliers and Category Management to ensure production capacity meets current and forecast demand.
- Lead supplier assessments, audits, and qualifications for new and existing suppliers.

Existing supplier capacity assessment
- Collaborate with suppliers and Category Management to ensure production capacity meets current and forecast demand.
- Anticipate and resolve bottlenecks or constraints that may impact delivery timelines.

Technology Roadmaps & Benchmarking
- Align supplier capabilities with product and technology roadmaps to drive innovation.
- Conduct benchmarking studies to evaluate market competitiveness of supplier pricing and services.

High-Level Expediting
- Support the procurement team in escalated material delays by driving quick-turn supplier engagement and recovery planning.
- Support Operations and Logistics on mission-critical supply continuity.

RFQ for New Parts & NPI Support
- Lead sourcing activities for new components, prototypes, and early-phase production tied to New Product Introductions (NPIs).
- Engage early with Engineering and Program Management to align sourcing plans with product timelines.

Supplier Business Reviews & Improvement
- Participate in periodic supplier business reviews focused on performance, risk, capacity, and collaboration opportunities.
- Support continuous improvement plans for underperforming suppliers and manage corrective actions.

Approved Supplier List & Preferred Part List
- Maintain and enforce compliance with the Approved Supplier List (ASL) and Preferred Part List (PPL).
- Partner with Engineering and Quality to update supplier and part approvals as needed.

Supplied Material Quality
- Work with suppliers and Quality to mitigate critical supplier quality events.
- Maintain the tooling and equipment asset management database.

Qualifications Required:
- Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, Engineering, Business, or a related field.
- 5+ years of strategic sourcing or procurement experience in a manufacturing environment.
- Experience with ERP systems (SAP preferred) and sourcing analytics tools.
- Strong contract negotiation and supplier relationship management skills.
- Solid understanding of cost modeling, value engineering, and total cost of ownership.

Preferred:
- Master’s degree or professional certifications (e.g., CPSM, CSCP, CPIM).
- Prior experience in sourcing engineered products, castings, electronics, or machined components.
- Experience supporting sustainability, compliance, and responsible sourcing initiatives.

Key Competencies:
- Strategic thinking and execution
- Strong analytical and financial acumen
- Cross-functional collaboration and influence
- Supplier engagement and development
- Problem-solving and decision-making under pressure
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

The estimated salary range for this position is $95,000 to $112,000 plus bonus.   Starting pay is dependent on multiple factors, such as skills, experience and work location, and is not typically at the top of the range.  At Xylem we offer a competitive compensation package with a generous benefit package, including Medical, Dental, Vision plans, 401(k) with company contribution, paid time off, paid parental leave and tuition reimbursement.

Xylem does not provide visa sponsorship for this position.

Job Summary:
The Operations Manager is responsible for overseeing the entire operational management system within the organization. This role involves developing and implementing operational policies and procedures, managing a team of operational professionals, and ensuring that operations meet or exceed customer expectations. The Operations Manager conducts regular audits, reviews operational performance data, and collaborates with other departments to drive continuous improvement initiatives. Key responsibilities include managing operational documentation, ensuring compliance with industry standards and regulations, and reporting on operational performance to senior leadership.
Responsibilities:

Strategic Planning
• Create and implement long-term business strategies
• Develop and monitor budgets and financial plans
• Analyze market trends and make recommendations for improvement
Project Management
• Oversee project timelines and ensure deadlines are met
• Coordinate with different departments to ensure smooth project execution
• Identify and resolve any project issues or conflicts

Supply Chain Management
• Manage inventory levels and ensure timely delivery of goods
• Negotiate contracts with suppliers and vendors
• Monitor and analyze supply chain processes for efficiency and cost-effectiveness

Quality Control
• Develop and enforce quality control procedures
• Conduct regular audits to ensure compliance with standards
• Address any quality issues and implement corrective actions

Risk Management
• Identify potential risks and develop contingency plans
• Ensure compliance with health and safety regulations
• Monitor and address any legal or regulatory issues

Customer Service
• Develop and maintain positive relationships with clients
• Address any customer complaints or concerns
• Implement strategies to improve customer satisfaction

Data Analysis and Reporting
• Track and analyze key performance indicators
• Generate reports on operations and present to upper management
• Use data to identify areas for improvement and make recommendations.

Team Management:
• Lead and manage a team, providing guidance, feedback, and support.
• Set goals and KPIs for team members and monitor performance.
• Foster a positive and collaborative work environment.
• Develop and implement training programs to keep team members updated on trends and strategies.

High Impact Behaviors:
• Strategic Decision Making: A manager must be able to assess complex situations, consider long-term implications, and make decisions that align with the organization’s vision and goals. This involves critical thinking, foresight, and the ability to balance various stakeholders’ interests.
• Effective Communication: Clear and transparent communication is vital for a manager. This includes articulating vision, expectations, and feedback in a way that motivates and engages team members. It also involves active listening and openness to input from all levels of the organization.
• Fostering Team Growth: A high impact manager invests in the development of their team members. This behavior includes mentoring, providing opportunities for professional growth, and creating an environment where continuous learning is encouraged and valued.

• Bachelor’s in Business Administration, Supply Chain Management, or related field, with at least 5 years experience., with at least 2 years experience as a people manager or equivalent work experience that provides exposure to fundamental theories, principles, and concepts.
• Proven experience in import/export operations with significant supervisory experience.
• Expert level understanding of advanced failure analysis techniques.
• Strong problem-solving and analytical skills to identify issues and develop effective solutions.
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills to report findings and make recommendations.
• Strong analytical skills to interpret complex data and translate it into actionable insights.
• Proficiency in data analysis tools and software, such as Excel, Google Analytics, and various CRM platforms.
• Experience with digital marketing strategies, including SEO, PPC, and SEM campaigns.
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present findings clearly and persuasively.
• A strategic thinker with a test and learn approach to marketing efforts and process improvements.
• Resource Allocation: Allocate personnel, tools, and other resources efficiently to achieve project goals. Balance competing priorities and adapt as needed.

jobs.title: Operations Director
jobs.description:
Xylem is a Fortune 500 global water solutions company dedicated to advancing sustainable impact and empowering the people who make water work every day. As a leading water technology company with 23,000 employees operating in over 150 countries, Xylem is at the forefront of addressing the world's most critical water challenges. We invite passionate individuals to join our team, dedicated to exceeding customer expectations through innovative and sustainable solutions.

Operations Director – Site Leadership & Transformation
Location:   Holland, MI   (relocation support available)
Reports to:   Vice President of Operations

The Opportunity
Xylem is seeking a   senior, hands‑on Operations Director   to lead site operations for a complex, high‑mix, low‑volume manufacturing facility supporting   Configure‑to‑Order (CTO) and Engineer‑to‑Order (ETO)   products. This role is designed for a proven operations leader who has successfully led   transformational change , built strong problem‑solving cultures, and delivered measurable improvements in safety, delivery, quality, and cost.
This is a true end‑to‑end site leadership role. The Operations Director owns operational performance and culture, leads strategy deployment, and works directly with teams on the floor to turn improvement plans into sustainable results. Success requires a leader who is comfortable at both the   strategic and tactical levels , and who leads by presence, action, and accountability.

What You Will Do
The Operations Director has full responsibility for site operations, including manufacturing, quality, materials, and logistics. The role leads daily execution while shaping the long‑term operational strategy, ensuring alignment with Xylem’s Lean Production System and enterprise objectives.
A major focus of the role is driving   site transformation —standardizing processes, improving flow, reducing lead times, and strengthening execution in a highly customized CTO/ETO environment. The Operations Director plays a visible, hands‑on role in embedding Lean principles such as standard work, visual management, and disciplined performance management.
This leader establishes and sustains a culture of structured problem solving, ensuring teams use tools such as A3 Thinking, PDCA, Kaizen, 8D, and DMAIC to address root causes and prevent recurrence. Operational KPIs—including safety, quality, on‑time delivery, productivity, cost, and lead time—are actively owned, reviewed, and improved.
The role partners closely with Engineering, Supply Chain, and Product Management to balance complexity, responsiveness, and cost competitiveness. Continuous improvement efforts focus on increasing production flexibility, strengthening planning and material flow, and selectively leveraging automation and digital tools where they add value.

People Leadership & Culture
Developing people and culture is central to success. The Operations Director leads, coaches, and mentors the site leadership team, building a strong pipeline of problem solvers and future leaders. Clear expectations, accountability, and engagement are reinforced at every level.
Safety leadership is non‑negotiable. The Operations Director sets the standard for a zero‑harm culture through visible leadership, disciplined processes, and employee involvement.
The role builds an environment of continuous learning and collaboration, strengthening Lean capability and ownership across hourly, professional, and leadership teams. The Operations Director partners with senior leadership on talent development, succession planning, and site growth initiatives.

Financial & Business Ownership
The Operations Director owns site financial performance, including operating budgets, cost control, and capital investment planning. This leader identifies and executes opportunities to improve cost efficiency while maintaining a strong customer experience and product quality.
Operational and financial targets are achieved through a combination of disciplined execution, process improvement, and strategic investment aligned with business priorities.

What You Bring
A successful candidate brings at least   10 years of progressive manufacturing operations leadership experience , ideally within a   high‑mix, low‑volume CTO/ETO environment . A bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Business, or a related field is required; an advanced degree is preferred.
This role requires demonstrated success leading   Lean transformations at the site level , with deep working knowledge of Lean production systems, structured problem solving, and continuous improvement methodologies. Strong experience in supply chain integration, production planning, and quality systems is essential.
The ideal candidate brings strong financial acumen, including experience managing operational budgets, cost reduction initiatives, and capital investments. Exceptional leadership, communication, and influencing skills are required, along with the ability to engage teams at every level of the organization.
Experience with ERP/MRP systems (such as SAP or Oracle), Lean or Six Sigma certification, and familiarity with ISO or regulated manufacturing environments are preferred.

Why Xylem
The compensation range for this position is $175,000-$215,000 and is based on multiple factors. Xylem offers the opportunity to lead meaningful transformation in a purpose‑driven organization that values operational excellence, accountability, and continuous improvement. The role includes a competitive compensation and benefits package, including Flexible Time Off (FTO), comprehensive health benefits, retirement savings plans, and relocation support.

jobs.title: Sr. Continuous Improvement Specialist
jobs.description:
Xylem is a Fortune 500 global water solutions company dedicated to advancing sustainable impact and empowering the people who make water work every day. As a leading water technology company with 23,000 employees operating in over 150 countries, Xylem is at the forefront of addressing the world's most critical water challenges. We invite passionate individuals to join our team, dedicated to exceeding customer expectations through innovative and sustainable solutions.

Xylem is looking for a   Senior Continuous Improvement Specialist   to help drive operational performance and Lean transformation at our   Cheektowaga manufacturing site in the Buffalo area . This is a strong opportunity for a   manufacturing engineer, industrial engineer, or continuous improvement professional   who wants to work in a visible, high-impact plant role where improvements on paper turn into measurable results on the floor.
This position supports the production of   industrial heat exchangers   serving a   rapidly growing data center market , giving the role a compelling mix of manufacturing complexity, business relevance, and long-term growth potential.
If you are energized by improving flow, increasing throughput, partnering with operations, and leading change in a real manufacturing environment, this role offers the chance to do that every day.

Why This Role Stands Out
This is not a desk-only CI role. You will spend a meaningful amount of time on the shop floor, working side by side with production teams, supervisors, and leadership to identify opportunities, solve problems, and sustain improvements. The role is ideal for someone who wants to move beyond analysis alone and directly influence how a plant performs.
You’ll have the chance to lead plant-level initiatives with visibility, ownership, and support from site leadership, while helping shape a culture of continuous improvement in a facility where hands-on engineering mindset and practical execution both matter.

What You’ll Do
In this role, you will lead cross-functional continuous improvement projects that improve   material flow, throughput, labor efficiency, and overall manufacturing performance . You’ll take projects from early-stage opportunity identification through implementation and sustainment, with a focus on driving measurable operational and financial results.
You will work closely with plant leaders and the union workforce to identify process constraints, reduce waste, improve workflow, and support better day-to-day execution across the facility. This includes helping teams address bottlenecks, strengthen standard work, and build more efficient and sustainable operating rhythms.
You’ll use   Lean, Six Sigma, and Kaizen tools   to solve complex manufacturing problems, while also using data and statistical analysis to support decisions and track results. Just as importantly, you’ll act as a change agent—building trust, gaining buy-in, and helping the site continue maturing its continuous improvement culture.
This role also offers the opportunity to coach others, share best practices, and strengthen CI capability across the organization.

What We’re Looking For
We’re looking for someone with a   Bachelor’s degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related technical field , along with   4+ years of experience in a manufacturing, industrial engineering, or continuous improvement role .
The strongest candidates will bring hands-on experience in plant environments and a track record of using   Lean, Six Sigma, and Kaizen methodologies   to improve performance. You should be comfortable using data to drive action, working across functions, and influencing both frontline teams and leadership.
This role is especially well suited for candidates who have worked in   heavy manufacturing ,   fabrication ,   industrial production , or similarly complex operational settings. Experience in a   unionized environment   is a strong plus.
We’re also looking for someone who is self-directed, pragmatic, and able to move initiatives forward with a high level of ownership. Strong communication and relationship-building skills are essential, as success in this role depends on both technical credibility and the ability to earn trust across the plant.
Preferred Qualifications
Preferred candidates may also have   Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification ,   PMP certification , or   ASQ credentials   such as   CQE   or   CMQ/OE . Experience with analytical tools such as   Minitab, JMP, or advanced Excel   is highly valued.

Work Environment
This role is   fully onsite   at our   Cheektowaga, NY facility   and requires a regular presence on the manufacturing floor. Approximately   25–50% of the role will be spent in the plant , supporting hands-on improvement efforts and collaborating directly with operations teams.

The Program Manager will be a dynamic individual with an entrepreneurial mindset that is not afraid to take the lead and become responsible for driving change to develop a stronger business.  In this role, the incumbent must be an objective thinker and problem solver, while processing the ability to solve challenging tasks to completion by building cooperative and influential relationships with numerous groups that impact the business on multiple levels.

The hiring team is primarily seeking candidates based in the Cheektowaga, NY area. Although this role is posted across multiple locations to identify qualified talent, the expectation is that the selected candidate will be based in Cheektowaga.

CORE RESPONSIBILITIES:   To perform the job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily.

- Independently manage medium-large size/complexity program(s).
- Accountable for program P&L including cost, schedule, technical performance across program lifecycle to meet customer and business commitments.
- Responsible for inspiring employees to achieve high performance, accountable for delivering growth, accomplishing business objectives, and ensuring the efficient deployment of internal investments.
- Primary customer liaison responsible for all program activities identifying customer gaps/needs and translating into new business opportunities.
- Effectively communicate with all internal and external stakeholders.
- Ability to develop and foster cross-business area collaboration.
- Work in a highly dynamic and changing environment and adapt to shifting customer priorities.
- Engage across the enterprise including Business Development, Finance, Engineering, and Operations.
- Integrate business acumen, value proposition, budget/funding options, competitive landscape, and business case development to inform business area pursuits and strategies.
- Working with the customer, will Design or offer solutions to the customers’ requirements.
- Contract Review management within the areas of focus.  Will be responsible for clarifying all customer requirements, proper negotiation of terms & conditions, project scope & documentation of customer acceptance.
- Customer Relationship Management – will be the primary point of contact with the customer regarding project updates, milestone changes and other related topics .
- Project Management of improvements to the overall effectiveness and efficiency of the order entry through shipping processes
- Working with the team will ensure there is a clearly defined Production Schedule and will ensure it is clearly communicated to the end customer and throughout the operation.
- Delivery of product to end customer.
- Additional duties and responsibilities may be required based upon organizational needs.

QUALIFICATIONS :
- Bachelor’s Degree and a minimum of 3 years of prior relevant experience
- Requires broad management and leadership knowledge to lead cross-department project teams or manage across the enterprise.
- Proficient at working with customers, including through challenging issues.
- Demonstrated process improvement experience.
- Program management experience with Department of Defense and/or knowledge of Nuclear Power preferred.
- PMP Certification preferred.
- Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal skills.
- U.S. Citizenship Required.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite, including Visio.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:
- Experience working within ASME welding standards , including interpretation and application of codes and quality requirements in regulated manufacturing or defense environments.
- Familiarity with NAVSEA (U.S. Navy) welding requirements , specifications, and documentation standards, including oversight of welding compliance on Navy programs.
- Exposure to Section VIII / Nuclear-related programs , including program execution in highly regulated, safety‑critical environments.
- Experience managing programs involving code‑driven fabrication, inspection, and compliance activities (e.g., welding procedures, qualifications, audits).
- Background supporting programs with DoD, Navy, or nuclear customers , particularly in environments requiring strict configuration control and documentation discipline.
- Ability to partner effectively with Engineering, Quality, and Operations teams to ensure compliance with welding and nuclear standards throughout the program lifecycle.

DAY IN THE LIFE :

In this role, the working environment is typical office and manufacturing floor environment.  In addition, this role may travel approximately 10%.

jobs.title: Sr. Continuous Improvement Specialist
jobs.description:
Xylem is a Fortune 500 global water solutions company dedicated to advancing sustainable impact and empowering the people who make water work every day. As a leading water technology company with 23,000 employees operating in over 150 countries, Xylem is at the forefront of addressing the world's most critical water challenges. We invite passionate individuals to join our team, dedicated to exceeding customer expectations through innovative and sustainable solutions.

At Xylem, we’re united by a shared purpose:   solving water challenges worldwide . As a global water technology leader, we create innovative solutions that help communities and industries transport, treat, analyze, and use water more efficiently.
We’re looking for a   Senior Continuous Improvement Specialist   to join our team in   Auburn, New York   and play a key role in advancing operational excellence across our production facility. This is an opportunity for a driven improvement leader to make a visible impact by leading strategic initiatives, strengthening Lean capabilities, and helping shape a culture of continuous improvement.
In this role, you’ll partner across functions to improve workflows, reduce waste, solve complex operational challenges, and deliver measurable results in cost, quality, and productivity.

What You’ll Do
As the Senior Continuous Improvement Specialist, you will lead high-impact efforts that improve performance and build long-term capability across the site. You’ll work closely with leaders and frontline teams to identify opportunities, implement practical solutions, and sustain results.
Your responsibilities will include leading cross-functional continuous improvement projects, streamlining manufacturing and business processes, and driving initiatives focused on labor reduction, waste elimination, inventory optimization, and cost savings. You’ll facilitate kaizen and rapid improvement events, apply Lean Six Sigma tools to solve root-cause issues, and support teams in removing barriers to performance.
You’ll also serve as a change agent across the organization by influencing stakeholders, challenging outdated practices, and helping foster a mindset of continuous learning and operational excellence. This role offers strong visibility and the opportunity to contribute beyond the Auburn site over time as part of Xylem’s broader continuous improvement journey.

What We’re Looking For
We’re seeking a candidate with a   Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical field , along with   1–5 years of experience in a manufacturing environment   using continuous improvement methodologies to deliver measurable business results.
The ideal candidate brings a strong understanding of Lean and CI tools, experience managing project plans for large-scale initiatives, and the ability to work effectively in dynamic or evolving environments. You should be confident leading change, influencing cross-functional teams, and communicating clearly with stakeholders at all levels.
A commitment to continued professional growth, including pursuit of advanced Lean or Six Sigma certifications, is important for success in this role.
Preferred Qualifications
Candidates will stand out if they have   Lean Six Sigma Green Belt, Black Belt, or Lean certification , as well as experience in   low-volume, high-mix manufacturing   such as machining, assembly, or welding. Experience in a   unionized environment , familiarity with   ERP/MRP systems , and advanced Microsoft Office skills, including   Project and Visio , are also valued. Experience with   VBA programming   or   database querying   is a plus.

Work Environment and Physical Requirements
This position is primarily office-based but requires a regular onsite presence within the manufacturing facility in Auburn, NY. The role includes routine movement throughout the facility, including standing, sitting, reaching, and bending, as well as light lifting of up to 20–25 pounds. Typical work hours are   40–45 hours per week , and travel is expected to be   less than 10% .

Why Join Xylem?
At Xylem, your work has purpose. You’ll be part of a company that is making a meaningful difference in the world by addressing critical water challenges through innovation and collaboration.
We also know that supporting our employees is essential to long-term success. That’s why we offer a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to support you professionally and personally. Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage beginning on day one, paid parental leave, fertility and maternity support, paid time off, company holidays, retirement savings with company contribution, tuition reimbursement, student loan support, emotional wellness resources, employee recognition programs, and opportunities to give back through volunteer initiatives like our Watermark program.

Compensation
The estimated salary range for this position is   $110,000 to $120,000 plus bonus . Starting pay is based on several factors, including experience, skills, and work location, and is not typically at the top of the range.

Additional Information
Xylem does   not provide visa sponsorship   for this position.
